{{< slidebreak >}}

::: notes
Let's make two generalizations. 
First, we let the hazard depend on some
covariates $x_1,x_2, \dots, x_p$; 
we will indicate this dependence by extending our notation for hazard:
:::

{{< include _subfiles/proportional-hazards-models/_sec-surv-conditional-hazards.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include _subfiles/proportional-hazards-models/_def-ph-model.qmd >}}

{{< slidebreak >}}


:::{#lem-diffloghaz-ph}

#### Difference of log-hazards between two covariate patterns

If $\loghaz(t|\vx) = \loghaz_0(t) + \reglincomb$, then:

$$
\ba
\diffloghaz(t|\vx: \vxs)
&= (\vx - \vxs) \cdot \vb
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

$$
\ba
\diffloghaz(t|\vx : \vxs)
&\eqdef \loghaz(t|\vx) - \loghaz(t|\vxs) && \text{(definition of log-hazard difference)} \\
&= \left[\loghaz_0(t) + \tp{\vx}\vb\right] - \left[\loghaz_0(t) + \tp{\vxs}\vb\right] && \text{(substituting model definition)} \\
&= \tp{\vx}\vb - \tp{\vxs}\vb && \text{(canceling shared baseline log-hazard } \loghaz_0(t)\text{)} \\
&= (\vx - \vxs) \cdot \vb && \text{(factoring out } \vb\text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-hazard-ratio-ph}

#### Hazard ratio under proportional hazards

If $\loghaz(t|\vx) = \loghaz_0(t) + \reglincomb$, then:

$$
\ba
\hr(t|\vx: \vxs)
&= \expf{\diffloghaz(t|\vx: \vxs)}
\\
&= \expf{(\vx - \vxs) \cdot \vb}
\\
&= \expf{\diffvx \cdot \vb}
\ea
$$

where $\diffvx \eqdef \vx - \vxs$ is the difference in covariate vectors.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

$$
\ba
\hr(t|\vx: \vxs)
&\eqdef \frac{\haz(t|\vx)}{\haz(t|\vxs)}
\\
&= \expf{\loghaz(t|\vx) - \loghaz(t|\vxs)}
\\
&= \expf{\diffloghaz(t|\vx: \vxs)}
\\
&= \expf{(\vx - \vxs) \cdot \vb}
\\
&= \expf{\diffvx \cdot \vb}
\ea
$$

Expanding the definition of $\hr$, the first equality writes the ratio
as the exponential of a difference of logarithms;
the second applies the definition of $\diffloghaz$ as that difference;
the third is @lem-diffloghaz-ph;
and the last substitutes $\diffvx$ for $\vx - \vxs$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

So for proportional hazards models, we can write the hazard ratio using a shorthand notation:

$$\hr(t| \vx : \vxs)  = \hr(\vx : \vxs)$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#lem-ph-diffloghaz-0}
#### Difference of log-hazard from baseline

$$\diffloghaz(t|\vx)= \reglincomb$${#eq-diffloghaz-0-ph}
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

$$
\ba
\diffloghaz(t|\vx)
&\eqdef \diffloghaz(t|\vx : \vzero) && \text{(definition of difference from baseline)} \\
&= (\vx - \vzero) \cdot \vb && \text{(applying @lem-diffloghaz-ph with } \vxs = \vzero\text{)} \\
&= \reglincomb && \text{(evaluating vector difference)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-hazard-ratio-vs-baseline-ph}

#### Hazard ratio versus baseline under proportional hazards

If $\loghaz(t|\vx) = \loghaz_0(t) + \reglincomb$, then:

$$\hazfactor(t|\vx) = \expf{\reglincomb}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

$$
\ba
\hazfactor(t|\vx)
&\eqdef \hr(t| \vx : \vzero) && \text{(definition of hazard factor)}
\\
&= \expf{\diffloghaz(t|\vx)} && \text{(applying @cor-hazard-ratio-vs-baseline)}
\\
&= \expf{\reglincomb} && \text{(substituting @lem-ph-diffloghaz-0)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-ph-haz-decomp}
#### Proportional-hazards decomposition of the hazard

$$\haz(t|\vx) = \haz_0(t)\hazfactor(\vx)$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

$$
\ba
\haz(t|\vx)
&= \expf{\loghaz(t|\vx)} && \text{(relationship between hazard and log-hazard)} \\
&= \expf{\loghaz_0(t) + \reglincomb} && \text{(substituting proportional hazards model)} \\
&= \expf{\loghaz_0(t)} \cdot \expf{\reglincomb} && \text{(exponent rule for sums)} \\
&= \haz_0(t) \hazfactor(\vx) && \text{(definitions of baseline hazard } \haz_0(t) \text{ and hazard factor } \hazfactor(\vx)\text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

{{< include _subfiles/proportional-hazards-models/_def-risk-score.qmd >}}

Also:

:::{#thm-ph-also}

#### Equivalent forms of the proportional-hazards model

$$
\ba
\hazfactor(\vx) &= \expf{\diffloghaz(\vx)}
\\
\logf{\haz(t|\vx)}
&= \logf{\haz_0(t)} + \diffloghaz(\vx)
\\
&= \loghaz_0(t) + \diffloghaz(\vx)
\\
\diffloghaz(\vx) &= \reglincomb \\
&\eqdef \beta_1x_1+\cdots+\beta_px_p
\ea
$$

:::

::: notes
This model is **semi-parametric**,
because the linear predictor depends on estimated
parameters but the base hazard function is unspecified.
There is no constant term in $\eta(x)$,
because it is absorbed in the base hazard.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

Alternatively, we could define $\beta_0(t) = \logf{\haz_0(t)}$, and then:

$$\eta(x,t) = \beta_0(t) + \beta_1x_1+\cdots+\beta_px_p$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: notes
For two different individuals
with covariate patterns $\vx_1$ and $\vx_2$,
the ratio of the hazard functions
(a.k.a. **hazard ratio**, a.k.a. **relative hazard**) is:
:::

$$
\ba
\frac{\haz(t|\vx_1)}{\haz(t|\vx_2)}
&=\frac{\haz_0(t)\hazfactor(\vx_1)}{\haz_0(t)\hazfactor(\vx_2)}\\
&=\frac{\hazfactor(\vx_1)}{\hazfactor(\vx_2)}\\
\ea
$$

::: notes
Under the proportional hazards model,
this ratio (a.k.a. proportion) does not depend on $t$.
This property is a structural limitation of the model;
it is called the **proportional hazards assumption**.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#def-pha}
#### Proportional hazards

A conditional probability distribution $p(T|X)$
has **proportional hazards** if the hazard ratio $\haz(t|\vx_1)/\haz(t|\vx_2)$
does not depend on $t$.
Mathematically, it is defined as:

$$
\frac{\haz(t|\vx_1)}{\haz(t|\vx_2)}
\eqdef \hr(\vx_1,\vx_2)
$$

:::

::: notes
Cox's proportional hazards model has this property, with $\hr(\vx_1,\vx_2) = \frac{\hazfactor(\vx_1)}{\hazfactor(\vx_2)}$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-haz-ratio-notations}

#### Relating the hazard-ratio and hazard-factor notations

::: notes
We are using two similar notations,
$\hr(\vx,\vxs)$ and $\hazfactor(\vx)$.
We can link these notations:
$$\hazfactor(\vx) \eqdef \hr(\vx, \vzero)$$

Then:
:::

$$\hr(\vx, \vxs) = \frac{\hazfactor(\vx)}{\hazfactor(\vxs)}$$
$$\hazfactor(\vzero) = \hr(\vzero, \vzero) = 1$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

$$
\ba
\hr(\vx, \vxs)
&= \frac{\haz(t|\vx)}{\haz(t|\vxs)} && \text{(definition of hazard ratio)} \\
&= \frac{\haz_0(t)\hazfactor(\vx)}{\haz_0(t)\hazfactor(\vxs)} && \text{(applying @thm-ph-haz-decomp)} \\
&= \frac{\hazfactor(\vx)}{\hazfactor(\vxs)} && \text{(canceling baseline hazard } \haz_0(t)\text{)}
\ea
$$

Setting $\vx = \vzero$ yields:

$$
\hazfactor(\vzero)
\eqdef \expf{\vzero \cdot \vb}
= e^0
= 1
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

The proportional hazards model also has additional notable properties:

$$
\ba
\frac{\haz(t|\vx_1)}{\haz(t|\vx_2)}
&=\frac{\haz_0(t)\hazfactor(\vx_1)}{\haz_0(t)\hazfactor(\vx_2)} && \text{(applying @thm-ph-haz-decomp)} \\
&=\frac{\hazfactor(\vx_1)}{\hazfactor(\vx_2)} && \text{(canceling baseline hazard } \haz_0(t)\text{)} \\
&=\frac{\expf{\eta(\vx_1)}}{\expf{\eta(\vx_2)}} && \text{(substituting hazard factor definition)} \\
&=\expf{\eta(\vx_1)-\eta(\vx_2)} && \text{(quotient rule for exponentials)} \\
&=\expf{\tp{\vx_1}\vb-\tp{\vx_2}\vb} && \text{(substituting linear predictors)} \\
&=\expf{\tp{(\vx_1 - \vx_2)}\vb} && \text{(factoring out } \vb\text{)}
\ea
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

Hence on the log scale, we have:

:::{#thm-diff-loghaz-lincom}
#### Difference of log-hazards is a linear combination

$$
\ba
\logf{\frac{\haz(t|\vx)}{\haz(t|\vxs)}}
&= \logf{\haz(t|\vx)} - \logf{\haz(t|\vxs)} && \text{(logarithm of quotient rule)}
\\
&\eqdef \loghaz(t|\vx) - \loghaz(t|\vxs) && \text{(definition of log-hazards)}
\\
&= \diffloghaz(t|\vx : \vxs) && \text{(definition of log-hazard difference)}
\\
&= \eta(\vx) - \eta(\vxs) && \text{(linear predictor form)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\vb - \tp{\vxs}\vb && \text{(substituting linear predictors)}
\\
&= \tp{(\vx - \vxs)}\vb && \text{(factoring out } \vb\text{)}
\ea
$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

Applying the [general procedure for interpreting a regression coefficient](Linear-models-overview.qmd#def-coef-interp-procedure) to the log-hazard linear predictor $\eta(\vx) = \diffloghaz(\vx) = \reglincomb$ (differentiating or differencing with respect to $x_j$, depending on whether $x_j$ is continuous or discrete, with all other covariates held fixed) yields the following interpretation of $\b_j$:

If only one covariate $x_j$ is changing, then:

$$
\ba
\logf{\frac{\haz(t|\vx_1)}{\haz(t|\vx_2)}}
&=  (x_{1j} - x_{2j}) \cdot \beta_j\\
&\propto (x_{1j} - x_{2j})
\ea
$$

::: notes
Specifically, under Cox's model $\haz(t|\vx) = \haz_0(t)\expf{\tp{\vx}\vb}$, the log of the hazard ratio is proportional to the difference in $x_j$, with the proportionality coefficient equal to $\beta_j$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

Further,

$$
\ba
\logf{\haz(t|\vx)}
&=\logf{\haz_0(t)}  + \reglincomb
\ea
$$

::: notes
This additive structure means that covariate effects are additive on the log-hazard scale;
hazard functions for different covariate patterns should be vertical shifts of each other.

See also:

<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proportional_hazards_model#Why_it_is_called_%22proportional%22>

:::

### Additional properties of the proportional hazards model

If $\haz(t|\vx)= \haz_0(t)\hazfactor(\vx)$, then:

:::{#thm-ph-cuhaz}

#### Cumulative hazards are also proportional to $\cuhaz_0(t)$

$$
\ba
\cuhaz(t|\vx)
&\eqdef \int_{u=0}^t \haz(u)du\\
&= \int_{u=0}^t \haz_0(u)\hazfactor(\vx)du\\
&= \hazfactor(\vx)\int_{u=0}^t \haz_0(u)du\\
&= \hazfactor(\vx)\cuhaz_0(t)
\ea
$$

where $\cuhaz_0(t) \eqdef \cuhaz(t|\vzero) = \int_{u=0}^t \haz_0(u)du$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-log-cuhaz-parallel}

#### The logarithms of cumulative hazard should be parallel

$$
\logf{\cuhaz(t|\vx)} =\logf{\cuhaz_0(t)}  + \reglincomb
$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

$$
\ba
\logf{\cuhaz(t|\vx)}
&= \logf{\hazfactor(\vx)\cuhaz_0(t)} && \text{(applying @thm-ph-cuhaz)} \\
&= \logf{\cuhaz_0(t)} + \logf{\hazfactor(\vx)} && \text{(logarithm of product rule)} \\
&= \logf{\cuhaz_0(t)} + \logf{\expf{\reglincomb}} && \text{(substituting definition of } \hazfactor(\vx)\text{)} \\
&= \logf{\cuhaz_0(t)} + \reglincomb && \text{(simplifying } \log(\exp(\cdot))\text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#cor-log-nlog-surv}
#### Linear model for log-negative-log survival
$$
\logf{-\logf{\surv(t|\vx)}} = 
\logf{-\logf{\surv_0(t)}}  + \reglincomb
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

$$
\ba
\logf{-\logf{\surv(t|\vx)}}
&= \logf{\cuhaz(t|\vx)} && \text{(since } -\log \surv(t|\vx) = \cuhaz(t|\vx)\text{)} \\
&= \logf{\cuhaz_0(t)} + \reglincomb && \text{(applying @thm-log-cuhaz-parallel)} \\
&= \logf{-\logf{\surv_0(t)}} + \reglincomb && \text{(substituting baseline cumulative hazard } \cuhaz_0(t) = -\log \surv_0(t)\text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-ph-surv}
#### Survival functions are exponential multiples of $\surv_0(t)$

$$\surv(t|\vx) = \sb{\surv_0(t)}^{\hazfactor(\vx)}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof
$$
\ba
\surv(t|\vx)
&= \expf{-\cuhaz(t|\vx)} && \text{(definition of survival function in terms of cumulative hazard)} \\
&= \expf{-\hazfactor(\vx)\cdot \cuhaz_0(t)} && \text{(applying @thm-ph-cuhaz)} \\
&= \paren{\expf{- \cuhaz_0(t)}}^{\hazfactor(\vx)} && \text{(power rule for exponents } e^{ab} = (e^a)^b\text{)} \\
&= \sb{\surv_0(t)}^{\hazfactor(\vx)} && \text{(substituting baseline survival } \surv_0(t) \eqdef \expf{-\cuhaz_0(t)}\text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
